s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neck pain with radiating pain and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Electrical pain radiating to the left hand
Weakness in fine movements and weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
key_facts: 6-month history of progressive neck pain
Pain radiates to the left hand
Numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes
Weakness in fine movements and weak grip of the left hand
Atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
Motor testing of the left hand revealed muscle strength of 3/5
Marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra on CT
Lesion involves the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments
Lesion does not significantly compromise the thecal sac
Lesion is intermediate to low signal on T1-weighted images and intermediate on T2-weighted images
Lesion shows heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, lesion involves the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments, and heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Similar imaging features, such as osteolysis and fluid-fluid levels, could be present in this case, although the absence of a clear fluid-fluid level on MRI makes this diagnosis less likely

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Midline location and involvement of the vertebral body are consistent with chordoma, although the lack of a clear description of a midline mass or sacral involvement makes this diagnosis less likely

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesion with vertebral body collapse and soft tissue component could be consistent with plasmacytoma, although the absence of systemic symptoms or other lytic lesions makes this diagnosis less likely

shortlist.label: Metastatic disease
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesion with vertebral body collapse and soft tissue component could be consistent with metastatic disease, although the absence of a known primary malignancy or other metastatic lesions makes this diagnosis less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, along with the lesion's imaging characteristics (intermediate to low signal on T1-weighted images, intermediate on T2-weighted images, and heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration), are consistent with a giant cell tumor of bone. Additionally, the involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments without significant compromise of the thecal sac and the clinical presentation of progressive neck pain radiating to the left hand with associated numbness and weakness also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Although considered due to similar imaging and histologic features, it was excluded based on specific distinguishing characteristics

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Not directly supported by the provided imaging characteristics and clinical presentation

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with different imaging features and is less likely to cause the specific pattern of neurological symptoms described

rejected.label: Metastatic disease
rejected.why: While possible, the specific combination of imaging findings and clinical presentation makes giant cell tumor of bone a more likely diagnosis
